comments.author: aleynaakyuz
comments.body:
Standard injection examples run smoothly. However, I also tuned the parameters in a way that posterior reaches the edge of the table. Then I calculated the likelihood of 600 posterior samples with master's and this PR's interpolant, and compared each to the same distance sum done directly without the table. With this PR, 75 of the 600 samples had a likelihood off by more than a factor of 1.6, and 25 by more than a factor of 2 (worst: 11×). On master it was 1 of 600 (worst: 3.2×). 

Usually, we do not sample near the edges so it is not a big deal but adding padding to the grid should improve the issue.

I also left a comment where I think it is a typo.

comments.body: Here's a further explainer why this is needed. One might ask, why not just use the 'nearest' mode. Is that not the same? This block is primarily useful when doing the 'floor' rounding. If you do then depending on the situation you might get a different length in the same situation. This is intended to make it more robust against this scenario.
